summary: 1931-32 two-story lookout above Janesville in Plumas NF, with a Cold War radar annex below it; seasonally staffed and reached by a 4WD road.

facts.design: Two-story summit lookout (completed 1932 per Summit Post); the register calls it an R1 design, a Region 1 revision of the California Region 4AR

access.note: Reached by a seasonal four-wheel-drive road; the lookout and access road were closed for construction in August and September 2016.

visit.trail_note: Seasonal 4WD road, NFS Road 28N02A, on the mountain's southeast slopes; check road conditions first.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Plumas National Forest

events.note: Construction began 1931; register says opened June 1931; Summit Post says completed 1932
Harry Foster at the lookout station by September 1931
Logging-truck fire south of the peak burned nearly 600 acres; lookout reported it
One of the forest's 19 lookouts stayed open in October 1945 to watch the Honey Lake slope
Air Force gap-filler radar annex on the summit fully functional; operated until 1967 (Summit Post)
Reported vandalized in June 1991; damage not estimated
Lookout and access road closed August 3 to September 30 for construction; fire watch coverage not expected to be affected

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says constructed and opened June 1931; Summit Post says construction began in 1931 and the two-story lookout was completed in 1932; 1931 newspapers show work still under way in July. The 1931 start agrees across sources; completion falls in 1931 or 1932.

The register gives 1958 to 1970 for the radar facility; Summit Post says it was fully functional by 1960 and operated until 1967; the Peakbagging caption gives 1960 to 1967. Two sources put the end at 1967.

notes_for_editor: Record built year 1931 stands as the start of construction; the completion year (1931 or 1932) is worth a human look. Radar end year is disputed (1967 vs 1970). Peakbagging's claim that the lookout was used in WWII for enemy plane spotting is unsourced and left out. No source found confirms staffing or road status after 2012; a 2024-25 search returned only general fire-season news. A Lassen News item on the Thompson Peak Initiative (a Cal Fire grant) appeared in search results and was not read.
